Edit one or more issues within the same repository.

Editing issues' projects requires authorization with the `project` scope.
To authorize, run `gh auth refresh -s project`.

Use `--attach` to upload an image or video to a single issue. Without a body
flag the issue keeps the body it already has and the attachment is appended to it.
If the body references an attached file, such as `![alt](./login.png)`, that
reference is rewritten to point at the uploaded asset instead. Paths in a
`--body-file` are relative to its directory, falling back to the working directory.
You can attach up to 50 files per command.

Alt text for an image follows the path after `#`, as in
`--attach './login.png#The login error state'`. Without it the filename is used.
A reference already in the body keeps the alt text written there. Video renders
as a player and has no alt text, so it cannot be given any.

If some attachments upload and others fail, the issue is still updated with the
ones that succeeded. The command then exits with a non-zero status, but the edited
issue URLs are still printed to stdout.

gh_edit_help:
Edit one or more issues within the same repository.

Editing issues' projects requires authorization with the `project` scope.
To authorize, run `gh auth refresh -s project`.

Use `--attach` to upload an image or video to a single issue. Without a body
flag the issue keeps the body it already has and the attachment is appended to it.
If the body references an attached file, such as `![alt](./login.png)`, that
reference is rewritten to point at the uploaded asset instead. Paths in a
`--body-file` are relative to its directory, falling back to the working directory.
You can attach up to 50 files per command.

Alt text for an image follows the path after `#`, as in
`--attach './login.png#The login error state'`. Without it the filename is used.
A reference already in the body keeps the alt text written there. Video renders
as a player and has no alt text, so it cannot be given any.

If some attachments upload and others fail, the issue is still updated with the
ones that succeeded. The command then exits with a non-zero status, but the edited
issue URLs are still printed to stdout.

The `--add-assignee` and `--remove-assignee` flags both support
the following special values:
- `@me`: assign or unassign yourself
- `@copilot`: assign or unassign Copilot (not supported on GitHub Enterprise Server)


USAGE
  gh issue edit {<numbers> | <urls>} [flags]

FLAGS
      --add-assignee login         Add assigned users by their login. Use "@me" to assign yourself, or "@copilot" to assign Copilot.
      --add-blocked-by number      Add 'blocked by' relationships by issue number or URL
      --add-blocking number        Add 'blocking' relationships by issue number or URL
      --add-label name             Add labels by name
      --add-project title          Add the issue to projects by title
      --add-sub-issue number       Add sub-issues by number or URL
      --attach file                Attach an image or video file, in '<file>#<image alt text>' format
  -b, --body string                Set the new body.
  -F, --body-file file             Read body text from file (use "-" to read from standard input)
  -m, --milestone name             Edit the milestone the issue belongs to by name
      --parent number              Set the parent issue by number or URL
      --remove-assignee login      Remove assigned users by their login. Use "@me" to unassign yourself, or "@copilot" to unassign Copilot.
      --remove-blocked-by number   Remove 'blocked by' relationships by issue number or URL
      --remove-blocking number     Remove 'blocking' relationships by issue number or URL
      --remove-label name          Remove labels by name

      --remove-parent              Remove the parent issue

Verify the installed Claude Code package through its documented lifecycle and Backplane conformance checks.

## Bounded Scope

### Allowed

- Complete and replay native guide commands for repeat install, pinned update, rollback to the recorded prior revision, and Backplane-only uninstall.
- Verify before/after identity and preservation for each operation, including unrelated plugins, user files, upstream Superpowers, repository history, and GitHub issue state.
- Run all five named Backplane conformance checks and authorized issue-state scenarios against disposable or explicitly authorized issues.

### Out of Scope

- Change the approved host contract or silently update/remove upstream.
- Run mutation scenarios on production issues without authorization.
- Claim rollback when the previous version cannot be restored and verified.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Repeat install remains one effective Backplane installation; a pinned update reaches the selected revision; rollback restores the recorded prior revision and required discovery; uninstall removes only Backplane-owned state.
- The exact guide commands pass in a disposable Claude Code profile. Failed candidate preflight leaves the prior verified installation available where restoration is supported, with a specific recovery action.
- Fresh sessions after applicable operations discover upstream using-superpowers and both Backplane skills from separate packages; all five conformance checks and authorized read-only, selection, design, readiness, execution, blocked/resume, review, and verified-completion scenarios are scored.

## Verification Seams

- Record Claude Code version, Backplane before/candidate/restored revisions, upstream source and revision, gh capability, three installed skill identities, and PASS/FAIL/UNKNOWN per operation and check.
- Run skill-structure, native-issue-intake, language-neutral-verification, lifecycle-transitions, and superpowers-installation with their mapped scenario rubrics.
- Prove zero issue mutation for read-only/selection; one correct Backplane label on each open tracked test issue; unrelated labels preserved; completed closure only after integrated evidence. Compare unrelated plugin, user-file, and upstream identity before and after every lifecycle operation.

Functional design: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-19-v0.1-adoption-installation-contract-design.md (approved 2026-09-19).
Rescope design: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-19-host-installation-leaf-rescoping-design.md.

The September27 draft and recovered October24 branch plan/evidence remain historical context. Publication of the plan is not lifecycle completion; #19 remains in design preparation until readiness prerequisites are verified.

Integrated evaluation: [Issue #19 satisfaction assessment](https://github.com/tvproductions/superpowers-backplane/blob/cde87943bdac5e92cab2eb21c2685251f7aab5d1/tests/scenarios/2026-10-25-issue-19-satisfaction.md) evaluates delivery `7d7ecac36f8dc74ce1a0895ab934468332f92f53` from merged PR #36. Its evidence storage commit `cde87943bdac5e92cab2eb21c2685251f7aab5d1` is distinct from the tested delivery. The earlier design-preparation statement is historical.
